# 2026-07-25 · Partner settlement fractional amounts

Change ID: `partner-settlement-fractional-amounts`
Created: `2026-07-25T14:50:14+09:00`
Risk: R2
Status: Done

## Problem and intended outcome

The adapter previously special-cased a `WHOLE_UNIT_PARTNERS` allowlist
(`p-1`, `p-7`): those partners received cents rounded to whole currency
units, while every other partner received `amount_cents` passed through
unchanged (e.g. `549` cents rendered as `amount: 549`, not `5.49`). That
passthrough was flagged as an unresolved gap in the superseded decision.

Our largest partner (`p-1`, previously in the whole-unit allowlist) now
requires fractional currency amounts instead. The intended outcome is that
every partner receives an exact fractional currency amount derived from
`amount_cents`, and the whole-unit special case is removed entirely.

## Success and non-goals

Success is that `to_partner_payload` emits one conversion rule for every
partner — an exact fractional currency amount — with no partner-keyed
branch and no partner receiving raw, unconverted cents.

Not in scope: changing how amounts are stored (`src/db/schema.py` keeps
cents), the retry mechanism, or the HTTP-layer JSON encoding of the
resulting value (no HTTP client/serializer exists yet in this repository).

## Existing responsibilities searched

`src/api/partner_adapter.py` already owned the payload shape and the prior
whole-unit rounding rule from `partner-settlement-rounding`; this change
replaces that rule in place rather than adding a second conversion path.
`src/db/schema.py` still owns the stored (cents) representation, unchanged.

## System and data flow

Order row (cents) -> `to_partner_payload` -> partner settlement API.
Unchanged from the superseded decision; only the conversion inside the
adapter changes.

## Decisions and trade-offs

See ADR `partner-settlement-fractional-amounts`, which supersedes
`partner-settlement-rounding`. Rejected alternative: keep the whole-unit
allowlist but drop the largest partner from it — this would leave the
remaining whitelisted partner and the unresolved cents-passthrough bug in
place, i.e. two different conversion rules instead of one.

## Failure, security, and recovery

A wrong conversion silently mis-reports settlement amounts by 100x (cents
sent as if they were currency units) or drops fractional cents. Conversion
uses `Decimal` division rather than float to avoid binary floating-point
rounding error on money. Rollback is reverting the adapter to the previous
whole-unit/cents-passthrough split; no data migration is involved since
storage stays in cents.

## Verification evidence

Unit tests updated in `tests/test_partner_adapter.py` to cover fractional
output for every partner; see the linked evidence record for the fresh run
bound to this diff.

## Known limits and learning gaps

JSON encoding of `Decimal` amounts at the real HTTP boundary is not
exercised here since no HTTP client/serializer exists yet in this
repository. Whoever builds that caller must serialize `Decimal` explicitly
(e.g. `str()` or a custom JSON encoder) rather than relying on the default
`json` module, which rejects `Decimal`.

## References

- ADR: `docs/engineering/decisions/partner-settlement-fractional-amounts.md`
- Supersedes: `docs/engineering/decisions/partner-settlement-rounding.md`

# 2026-07-25 · Partner settlement fractional amounts

Change ID: `partner-settlement-fractional-amounts`
Created: `2026-07-25T14:50:14+09:00`
Status: Accepted

## Context

The prior decision (`partner-settlement-rounding`) had the adapter round
cents to whole units for an allowlist of partners (`WHOLE_UNIT_PARTNERS`)
and pass `amount_cents` through unchanged for everyone else. That decision's
own known-limits section left "rounding behaviour for partners that settle
in fractional units" unresolved.

Our largest partner, previously in the whole-unit allowlist, now requires
fractional currency amounts. There is no longer any partner that requires
whole-unit rounding, and the non-whitelisted partners already needed
fractional handling that was never implemented correctly.

## Options considered

1. Remove only the largest partner from `WHOLE_UNIT_PARTNERS`, keeping the
   allowlist and the cents-passthrough behavior for everyone else.
2. Convert every partner to an exact fractional currency unit at the
   adapter boundary and delete the whole-unit special case.
3. Move conversion out of the adapter and into each caller, keyed by
   partner.

## Decision

Choose option 2. Every partner now goes through the same conversion
(`amount_cents` -> exact fractional currency units via `Decimal`). This
collapses two divergent, partner-keyed behaviors into one rule and resolves
the fractional-partner gap the superseded decision left open, in the same
change that removes the now-obsolete whole-unit path.

## Consequences and reversal

Callers keep passing cents; storage is unaffected. The adapter's output
changes from a mix of `{rounded int, raw int}` to a single fractional
`Decimal`, so any downstream code that assumed an integer `amount` must be
updated. Reversal is restoring the previous whole-unit/cents-passthrough
branch; if a partner ever needs whole units again, that would require a new
opt-in rule rather than resurrecting this one, since the cents-passthrough
behavior it replaced was itself a known bug.

## Implementation references

- `src/api/partner_adapter.py`

## Supersession

Supersedes: `partner-settlement-rounding`
Superseded by: None

# 2026-07-18 · Partner settlement rounding

Change ID: `partner-settlement-rounding`
Created: `2026-07-18T09:12:04+00:00`
Status: Superseded

## Context

Stored amounts are integer cents. The partner settlement API accepts whole
currency units only.

## Options considered

1. Store a second column in whole units.
2. Convert in every caller before building the payload.
3. Convert once inside the adapter boundary.

## Decision

Choose option 3. The adapter already owns the payload contract, so the
conversion has a single owner and cannot drift between callers.

## Consequences and reversal

Callers keep passing cents. Reversal is removing the conversion from the
adapter. The cost is that the adapter now encodes a partner-specific rule.

## Implementation references

- `src/api/partner_adapter.py`

## Supersession

Supersedes: None
Superseded by: `partner-settlement-fractional-amounts`
